title: Bangladesh to support revival of shuttered industries with $1.63 bn
summary:
Bangladesh Bank has launched a $1.63 billion pre-finance scheme to revive closed or sick large industrial and service-sector enterprises.
Companies with the technical skills, infrastructure, and commercial capacity to take over or lease a closed unit and restart operations will also receive priority.
Loan defaulters, money launderers, fund diverters and fraudsters will be barred from the low-cost loans.

title: Sweden’s H&M Foundation unveils 2026 Global Change Award winners
summary:
H&M Foundation’s Global Change Award 2026 recognises 10 innovators tackling fashion’s highest-emission areas through bio-based fibres, textile recycling, AI-driven efficiency and low-impact dyeing. 
Winners from India, the US, UK, Sweden, France, Tanzania and Bangladesh will each receive €200,000 and join a year-long programme supporting scalable climate solutions for a net-zero textile industry by 2050.

title: Egyptian cotton traceability reset: Why buyers are paying more
summary:
Egyptian cotton is undergoing a strategic reset as buyers increasingly demand verified origin, traceability and contamination control alongside fibre quality. 
While Giza cotton continues to command a premium, that advantage is narrowing. 
With stricter sustainability rules, Egypt is focusing on traceable, value-added cotton products to strengthen competitiveness and support export growth.

title: India’s polyester market sees mixed trend amid crude oil volatility
summary:
India’s polyester raw material market showed mixed trends this week as volatile crude oil prices, driven by Middle East war, influenced sentiment.
PTA rose ₹3/kg and melt increased ₹2.58/kg, while MEG remained stable.
Polyester yarn producers raised prices amid higher input costs, though downstream buyers continued cautious, need-based purchases amid uncertainty over feedstock and demand trends.

title: Australia to see cotton crop contract to 3 mn bales in 2026-27
summary:
With harvest completed in the north and nearing completion in the south, the 2025-26 production year for many Australian cotton growers has been a delicate balance of prioritising limited water supply and increasing costs, against what initially looked to be relatively low and flat price outlook, ANZ said.
The country may see a further contraction in cotton crop to 3 million bales for the 2026-27 season.

title: Oil crisis hits world growth outlook as Fitch revises down forecasts
summary:
World growth prospects have been hurt by the oil crisis triggered by the Middle East conflict, Fitch Ratings said.
It lowered its 2026 forecast for global growth by 0.2 pp to 2.4 per cent.
Forecast cuts have been widespread as higher inflation squeezes real wages, dampens consumption and raises companies’ input costs.
Growth in emerging markets excluding China has been lowered by 0.2 pp to 3.2 per cent.

title: Vietnam, Canada to shift to more substantive phase of cooperation
summary:
Vietnam and Canada have agreed to focus on three priority areas and shift from the JEC mechanism to a more action-oriented and substantive cooperation phase.
One of the priority areas is diversifying trade and investment, making effective use of the CPTPP, supporting an open trading system and accelerating ASEAN-Canada FTA talks.
Another is expanding cooperation in energy, infrastructure and green growth.

title: Rising energy prices push OECD headline inflation to 4.4% in April
summary:
YoY OECD CPI inflation rose to 4.4 per cent in April from 4 per cent in March.
Headline inflation rose in 23 OECD nations, stayed broadly stable in six and fell in nine.
OECD’s YoY energy inflation reached 13.2 per cent in April—up by 5.1 pp from March.
Thirty one out of 37 OECD countries with available data saw a rise in energy inflation.
Core inflation was broadly stable at 3.6 per cent.

title: Seasonally-adjusted GDP down 0.2% QoQ, up 0.3% YoY in euro area
summary:
In Q1 2026, seasonally-adjusted GDP decreased by 0.2 per cent quarter on quarter (QoQ) in the euro area and by 0.1 per cent in the EU, according to Eurostat. 
Denmark recorded the highest QoQ GDP rise. 
It increased by 0.3 per cent YoY in the euro area and by 0.7 per cent YoY in the EU in the quarter. 
Employment increased by 0.5 per cent YoY in both the euro area and the EU in the quarter.

title: Future Australian wool prices may stay at relatively high levels: ANZ
summary:
Australia’s wool market has stabilised across early- to mid-2026, with prices holding at relatively high levels compared with recent years and confidence improving after two volatile seasons in a row, an ANZ Bank report said.
Prices may remain at relatively high levels in future, but with greater variability from week to week.
Price movements continue to be somewhat volatile.

title: Tiruppur garment exports top $4.4 bn despite global trade challenges
summary:
Tiruppur’s garment exports stood at ₹42,544.40 crore ($4.4 billion) in fiscal 2025-26, down 4.91 per cent year on year due to US tariff issues and disruptions from the West Asia crisis, according to TEA.
Despite the decline, the knitwear hub remained resilient and sees growth opportunities through FTAs, MMF garments, sustainability initiatives, and rising export demand.

title: Cambodia’s clean-power garment premium
summary:
Cambodia is positioning clean energy as a sourcing advantage for its apparel industry, with renewables accounting for over 62 per cent of the power mix and solar capacity expanding rapidly. 
Energy audits highlight major cost and emissions-saving opportunities for factories. 
However, realising this potential will require wider renewable power access, financing, and credible low-carbon certification.

title: Australia’s apparel imports down 3.3%, textile import up in July-April
summary:
Australia’s apparel imports fell 3.3 per cent to Au$10.72 billion during July 2025-April 2026, while textile yarn, fabric and made-up article imports rose 1.6 per cent to Au$3.93 billion, according to ABS data.
Textile fibre imports also increased.
However, April 2026 saw declines in both apparel and textile imports, while textile fibre exports grew 4.9 per cent in the ten-month period.

title: Why Bangladesh RMG exporters feel April data needs July reality check
summary:
Bangladesh’s export earnings surged 32.92 per cent year on year in April, crossing the $4 billion mark, with apparel exports rising 31.21 per cent. 
However, exporters estimate actual growth at around 8–10 per cent, attributing the jump largely to delayed shipments after Eid disruptions.  
Industry stakeholders believe the true export trend will become clearer by July 2026.

title: Vietnam’s textile, garment exports reach $15.1 bn in January-May
summary:
Vietnam’s textile and garment exports (excluding yarn and fibre) edged up 0.4 per cent year-on-year to $15.13 billion during January-May 2026, while yarn exports rose 8.7 per cent to $1.89 billion.
Cotton imports fell 6.3 per cent in value despite higher volumes, and fabric imports eased 0.5 per cent.
The country is targeting $50 billion in textile, garment, and yarn exports in 2026.

title: US’ Torrid Q1 FY26 sales fall 7.6% despite guidance beat
summary:
Torrid Holdings reported first-quarter FY26 net sales of $245.8 million, down 7.6 per cent year-on-year, while net income fell to $0.4 million from $5.9 million. 
Comparable sales declined 1.7 per cent and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $17.6 million. 
The company closed 20 stores during the quarter and expects FY26 net sales between $940 million and $960 million.

title: Bangladesh garment exports slip to $35.3 bn in July-May
summary:
Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) exports fell 3.41 per cent year-on-year to $35.31 billion during July 2025-May 2026, with knitwear exports down 4.26 per cent and woven garments down 2.42 per cent.
Home textile exports rose 3.48 per cent to $853.26 million, while cotton product exports declined 11.23 per cent.
RMG and home textiles accounted for 82.57 per cent of the country’s total exports.

title: EU deadstock ban 2026: Fashion’s unsold inventory reckoning
summary:
From July 2026, large companies in the EU can no longer routinely destroy unsold apparel, footwear and accessories, shifting fashion towards stricter inventory accountability.
Backed by ESPR rules and upcoming disclosure mandates, brands must now prove how deadstock is reused, repaired, donated or recycled.
The change pressures forecasting, returns, traceability and resale systems.

title: Canada’s Lululemon reports mixed Q1 results, lowers FY26 outlook
summary:
Lululemon has reported mixed Q1 FY26 results, with net revenue rising 4 per cent to $2.5 billion, driven by 22 per cent international growth, while Americas revenue declined 3 per cent. 
Gross margin fell 410 basis points to 54.2 per cent and diluted EPS dropped to $1.69. 
The company lowered its FY26 outlook, citing macroeconomic headwinds and softer demand in the Americas market.

title: US’ Caleres reports strong Q1 FY26 growth led by Brand Portfolio
summary:
Caleres has reported Q1 FY26 net sales of $666.6 million, up 8.5 per cent YoY, driven by 20.6 per cent growth in its Brand Portfolio business. 
Adjusted EPS rose to $0.38, exceeding guidance, while gross margin improved 200 basis points to 47.3 per cent. 
Famous Footwear sales declined 2.5 per cent. 
The company expects modest sales growth and improved profitability for full-year FY26.
